new_entities.name: Low-dose CT lung screening in high-risk adults
aliases: high-risk low-dose CT lung cancer screening
new_entities.description: Low-dose computed tomography screening for lung cancer in adults at high smoking-related risk.

edges.effect_quant: The landmark NLST and NELSON trials both showed lower lung-cancer mortality with LDCT screening in high-risk populations, and the 2022 Cochrane review estimated a pooled 21% mortality reduction across randomized trials.
edges.population: current or former heavy smokers and other adults meeting high-risk eligibility criteria for lung cancer screening
edges.mechanism: LDCT screening shifts lung cancer diagnosis toward earlier, potentially curable stages before symptom-driven presentation, which is the main pathway by which it lowers lung-cancer death in high-risk groups.
edges.summary: This is one of the strongest adult cancer-screening mortality edges in modern screening literature. The evidence is good enough that the main debate is now about implementation, eligibility, false positives, and overdiagnosis rather than whether high-risk LDCT can reduce lung-cancer mortality at all.
edges.caveats: The benefit is specific to high-risk populations and should not be generalized to low-risk adults. False positives, incidental findings, and overdiagnosis remain important harms that are not encoded in this mortality-focused edge.

evidence.citation: National Lung Screening Trial Research Team 2011 N Engl J Med
evidence.notes: Reduced lung-cancer mortality with low-dose computed tomographic screening. NLST trial.

effect_quant.comparator: low-dose CT versus chest radiography in NLST for lung-cancer mortality

evidence.citation: deKoning HJ et al 2020 N Engl J Med
evidence.notes: Reduced Lung-Cancer Mortality with Volume CT Screening in a Randomized Trial. NELSON trial.

effect_quant.comparator: volume CT screening versus no screening at 10 years in NELSON

evidence.citation: Bonney A et al 2022 Cochrane Database Syst Rev
evidence.notes: Impact of low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) screening on lung cancer-related mortality.

effect_quant.comparator: LDCT screening versus control groups for lung cancer-related mortality
